researchQuestion: Can a bounded, text-only high-confidence detector recover enough invalidation events and predecessor links to remove Memora operation metadata from the runtime path?

dataset.name: Memora
dataset.deduplication: Use the ten quarterly persona histories only; do not count their weekly or monthly prefixes again.

personaSplits.rule: The detector and thresholds are fixed before aggregate scores are computed. Development examples may inform the rules; validation and test personas may not change them.

allowed: prior shared-memory text from the same persona

detector.precedence: delete cues outrank update cues when both occur
detector.exceptions: An exact quoted phrase or exact numeric token shared with a prior unit may satisfy the link threshold with one shared content token.
detector.complexityBound: At most 512 prior units are scored for one cue-bearing session and at most three predecessor links are emitted.

goldUse.scoringOnly: Released operation metadata is read only after prediction to derive gold invalidating sessions, event kind, obsolete values, and predecessor unit ids.
goldUse.goldEventDefinition: A session is positive only when the existing structured Memora adapter emits at least one update/delete event containing at least one obsolete value.
goldUse.goldLinkDefinition: A prior shared-memory unit is a gold predecessor when it predates the event and contains a normalized released obsolete value.

baselines.description: Predict deletion only for literal remove/delete/drop cues; no completion or update rules.
Apply the same cue classifier without requiring a predecessor link.
Emit an event only when a cue and a bounded predecessor link both exist.

decisionRule: D18 passes only when every linked_high_confidence test gate passes. Validation is descriptive and cannot relax the frozen test thresholds. A failure leaves V1 classified as oracle-management evidence and blocks any end-to-end correction-detection claim.
claimBoundary: This deterministic English detector targets explicit corrections and completions. Even a pass would not establish implicit code-state invalidation, repository scope, or human-level semantic linking. No answer-model calls are authorized by this protocol.
